work_items.title: Program.cs CLI hooks: `migrate` arg-subcommand (run EF migrations then exit) + `send-sms` arg-subcommand (real ISmsSender) — root of all Program.cs-touching WIs
work_items.goal: Two CLI arg-intercepts mirroring the existing create-superadmin pattern in Program.cs (SOURCE-VERIFIED lines 198-219: `if (args.Length > 0 && args[0] == ...)` after `builder.Build()`, run work in an async scope, `return;` before `app.Run()`; uses the existing private `GetArgValue(args, "--flag")` helper). (1) `dotnet run -- migrate`: resolve TaxiDbContext from a scope, call `await db.Database.MigrateAsync()`, log and `return;` before the web host boots. This is the deploy.yml migrate step (`compose run --rm api migrate` then `up`); LEAVE the existing Development-only startup MigrateAsync (lines 224-236) untouched — prod uses the explicit subcommand. (2) `dotnet run -- send-sms --to <e164> --message <text>`: resolve the NOTIFICATIONS ISmsSender (Taxi.Api.Infrastructure.Notifications.ISmsSender — the one with real GoSMS/SMSbrana providers, SendAsync(SmsMessage, ct) returning SmsSendResult — NOT the Infrastructure.Sms OTP sender), build an SmsMessage, send, log the outcome (never the message body or full phone — mask per rules/logging.md), `return;`. This WI is the ROOT of the Program.cs-touching chain: A2 (metrics) and A3 (5xx middleware) depend_on it so edits to Program.cs never collide (UC-007 ErrorCodes.cs-append precedent). No migration (no schema change). Test-first: the migrate subcommand is verified by the existing test harness still booting green + a documented `compose run` step; send-sms is unit/integration-tested by resolving a recording/console ISmsSender and asserting SendAsync was invoked with the parsed to/message, plus an arg-parsing test for missing flags.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet run -- migrate` intercepts args[0]=="migrate" after builder.Build(), runs `await db.Database.MigrateAsync()` in an async scope, logs a completion line, and returns before app.Run() (never boots the web host). The existing Development-only startup MigrateAsync block (Program.cs 224-236) is UNCHANGED. MigrateCommand_Intercepts_AndReturnsBeforeHostBoots is validated by the test harness booting green + documented `docker compose run --rm api migrate` runbook step.

`dotnet run -- send-sms --to <e164> --message <text>` resolves Taxi.Api.Infrastructure.Notifications.ISmsSender (the real-provider interface, SendAsync(SmsMessage, ct)), sends, logs the outcome, and returns before app.Run(). SendSms_ValidArgs_InvokesSmsSenderWithParsedToAndMessage passes by resolving a recording/console ISmsSender and asserting the SmsMessage carries the parsed --to/--message.

SendSms_MissingToOrMessage_LogsErrorAndReturns: absent --to or --message logs an error and returns (no send), mirroring create-superadmin's missing-flag guard. No message body or full phone number is logged (rules/logging.md — mask phone, use Reason).
dotnet build -warnaserror is clean and the full test suite stays green. No migration is added (no schema change).

LIBRARY RESEARCH (done 2026-09-13, cite in notes): prometheus-net.AspNetCore 8.2.1 is the current release and supports .NET 10 (preview 4+) — it is ASP.NET-Core-10 compatible; integration is `app.UseHttpMetrics()` (after routing/auth) + `app.MapMetrics()` (maps GET /metrics). DEVELOPER MUST re-confirm 8.2.1 restores cleanly under net10.0 at implementation time and bump to the then-current 8.x if a patch exists; pin an explicit version in the csproj. Wire `UseHttpMetrics()` and `MapMetrics("/metrics")` into Program.cs alongside the other app.Use*/Map* calls (place MapMetrics near the health-check Map* calls; UseHttpMetrics after UseAuthentication, consistent with existing middleware order). The endpoint returns 200 with Prometheus text-format body. SCOPE SPLIT (advisor): 'internal-network only' is NOT enforced in code — it is enforced by NOT proxying /metrics through Caddy and by compose network topology (that AC lives on C2, the Caddy/compose WI). The code AC here is only: endpoint served + scrapeable + default HTTP metrics registered. depends_on A1 to serialize Program.cs edits. No migration.
acceptance_criteria: prometheus-net.AspNetCore (version ~8.2.1, pinned explicitly; developer re-confirms net10.0 restore at impl time, bump within 8.x if a newer patch exists — cite version + date in the WI notes) is added to Taxi.Api.csproj and restores under -warnaserror.

Program.cs calls app.UseHttpMetrics() (after UseAuthentication, consistent with the existing middleware order) and app.MapMetrics("/metrics"). No auth/tenant coupling on /metrics (it is network-isolated, not authz-isolated); the endpoint does not require a JWT. 'Not publicly routable' is DEFERRED to C2 (Caddy does not proxy /metrics; compose keeps it on the internal network) — it is NOT an AC of this code WI.

work_items.title: 5xx-per-minute counter middleware + testable window alerter → ONE IPushSender push to FleetAdmins of the `ops` fleet when >10/min
work_items.goal: The cheapest-possible pager (assignment section 6 error-alerting). A middleware registered in Program.cs counts HTTP 5xx responses; a testable Common/Ops/FiveHundredRateAlerter (TimeProvider-driven, injectable) holds the decision logic: count 5xx within a rolling one-minute window; when the count crosses >10 in a window, fire EXACTLY ONE alert for that window, reset at the next window, and fire nothing when <=10. CRITICAL (advisor correction): the alert path is IPushSender, NOT INotificationService. INotificationService.NotifyAsync(evt, Order, ct) is order-coupled (routing keys off event+order) and a 5xx alert has no Order — using it will not compile. The correct path (mirrors NotificationService's recipient lookup, CLAUDE.md/UC-005): resolve the ops fleet by slug → its active FleetAdmin Users (IgnoreQueryFilters, u.FleetId == opsFleet.Id && u.IsActive && u.Role == UserRole.FleetAdmin) → their PushSubscription rows → Taxi.Api.Infrastructure.Notifications.IPushSender.SendAsync(subscription, PushMessage, ct) directly for each. SCOPE GAP (assumption, labeled): there is NO `ops` fleet concept in code (Explore confirmed; lookup is by Fleet.Slug only). The alerter looks up a fleet whose Slug == config `Ops:FleetSlug` (default "ops"); if the fleet or its FleetAdmin subscriptions are absent, it logs a Warning and no-ops (never throws — infra-alert failure must not cascade). This keeps alerting self-contained and cheap. depends_on A2 to serialize Program.cs edits. No migration. Test-first: the alerter decision logic is unit-tested against a FakeTimeProvider (11-in-a-window → one alert; next window resets; <=10 → none) with a recording IPushSender; an integration test seeds an ops fleet + FleetAdmin + PushSubscription and asserts one push is sent.
acceptance_criteria: A middleware counts HTTP 5xx responses and feeds a testable Common/Ops/FiveHundredRateAlerter driven by the injected TimeProvider. FiveHundredAlerter_ElevenIn60s_FiresExactlyOneAlert, FiveHundredAlerter_NextWindow_ResetsAndCanFireAgain, and FiveHundredAlerter_TenOrFewer_FiresNothing pass against a FakeTimeProvider.

The alert path is IPushSender.SendAsync(PushSubscription, PushMessage, ct) — NOT INotificationService. Recipients are the active FleetAdmin Users of the fleet whose Slug == Ops:FleetSlug (default "ops", IgnoreQueryFilters), via their PushSubscription rows. FiveHundredAlerter_SendsPushToOpsFleetAdmins seeds an ops fleet + FleetAdmin + subscription and asserts exactly one push per subscription via a recording IPushSender.

ASSUMPTION (labeled): no `ops` fleet exists in code; the slug is config-driven (Ops:FleetSlug). FiveHundredAlerter_NoOpsFleet_LogsWarningAndNoOps: when the ops fleet or its FleetAdmin subscriptions are absent, the alerter logs a Warning and sends nothing (never throws — infra-alert failure must not cascade, rules/error-handling.md).
No PII beyond ids in logs (rules/logging.md). dotnet build -warnaserror clean; full suite green. No migration.
